title: The decision flow: where decisions go and where they stop

sections.name: summary
sections.label: Summary
sections.content:
A section parallel to the work-flow map (The archetypal flow, container 165f3a6e), opened at the owner's request on 2026-10-28 (vignettes 3e076051, 6606adfe, 5f271974, e3069d0d). It zooms into work-flow stage 8, Decide, the way that map is fractal. Its working definition is the owner's: a decision is a choice that removes future choices, and it does so only at the level and in the domain where it is relevant. Elsewhere it is noise.

Six stages, a first pass by an agent (confidence low; untested), each an exercise that stops evidence:
1. Arise: a choice appears (issue, PR, review, conversation, session).
2. Settle by principle: a charter cell, ADR, ruling or principle already decides it (most stop here; finding e832c6f4).
3. Place: the level and boundary where it removes choices; nested and parallel domains are sensed here.
4. Decide: the owner of that level settles it (mode and door).
5. Record: one findable store, by stable id, never only in a branch or PR text.
6. Cite and revisit: later work references it; revisit_when; supersede; domains merge from experience.

Stops are findings tagged decision-stop that evidence the stage where the decision stopped (proposed decision, this conversation). Work flow and decision flow are read together.
